selectedCourses.name: Personal & Professional Development
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
selectedCourses.contribution: Mandatory first-year academic literacy and personal/professional development.
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

selectedCourses.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces financial accounting, management accounting and investment appraisal, including accounting's social role and accountability implications. Students record transactions, prepare and interpret financial statements, and analyze performance and financing. The course then examines costing, pricing, budgeting, organizational control and sustainable management accounting. Investment decisions are evaluated using accounting and discounted-cash-flow measures. A case study analyzes the misuse of an accounting principle and its financial-statement effects.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops accounting and financial-statement analysis for business decisions
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. Students learn how to comprehend a typical corporate annual report and to use accounting as a tool in understanding how economic events affect business.

selectedCourses.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. AI foundations and limitations lead into applications across enterprise functions and industries, labour-market change, productivity, innovation, market structure and inequality. Governance, corporate responsibility, regulation and future scenarios connect technological developments to institutional choices. Students analyze business cases and competing scholarly arguments, then investigate a country's AI readiness, workforce, regulation and industrial policy.
selectedCourses.contribution: examines managerial, organisational and societal implications of AI and technological change
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. Students study AI's capabilities and limits, applications across business functions and industries, and effects on labour markets, productivity, innovation and inequality. Business cases and scholarly arguments support analysis of governance, regulation and a country's AI readiness and industrial policy.

selectedCourses.name: Transnational Business Law
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Studies legal frameworks governing cross-border business transactions, combining comparative and international perspectives with practical legal problem-solving. Topics include trade regulation, contracts and international sales, transport and documentary transactions, finance, services, intellectual property, foreign investment and digital commerce. Advisory assignments assess contractual outcomes, risk allocation, intellectual-property protection and e-commerce compliance. A simulated arbitration develops written legal argument and oral advocacy.
selectedCourses.contribution: covers legal frameworks for contracts, trade, company activity and digital commerce across borders
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Transnational Business Law studies legal frameworks for cross-border business, including contracts, trade, intellectual property, foreign investment and digital commerce. Comparative and international perspectives support analysis of legal risks through discussions, problem-based assignments and an arbitration simulation.

reusedSharedDescriptionReview.reviewNote: Compared with the current selected workbook field. Retained the existing description as a faithful account; updated its source provenance.

selectedCourses.name: Money, Banking & Finance
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines financial markets and institutions, including the pricing of bonds, stocks and derivatives, interest rates and their risk and term structure, commercial-bank balance sheets and performance, financial structure and regulation, banking fragility and financial crises, central banks, money creation and monetary policy. Students apply algebraic and graphical analysis to financial and monetary problems. In the Stanford Banking Game they manage a simulated bank, analyse performance in Excel dashboards, forecast financial statements, and make evidence-based decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk. A small research project extends a selected financial or monetary research article through additional literature, a case study or updated evidence.
selectedCourses.contribution: Financial markets, securities, interest-rate risk, banks, regulation and monetary policy are applied in a bank-management simulation and a financial/monetary research extension. This directly supplies finance analysis, not a full accounting programme.
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Examines financial markets, commercial banks and central banks, including interest rates, financial regulation, financial crises and monetary policy. Students analyse financial problems and manage a simulated bank in the Stanford Banking Game, using Excel dashboards and financial forecasts to inform decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk.

reusedSharedDescriptionReview.reviewNote: Reviewed against the selected profile and current official description. Describes substantive financial and banking content and the bank-management simulation without treating the source as proof of future delivery.

selectedCourses.name: Introduction to Economics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces microeconomic principles and short-run macroeconomic analysis. The microeconomic component examines supply and demand, strategic interaction, consumer choice, production, costs and competitive markets. The macroeconomic component introduces output, unemployment and inflation, then relates goods and financial markets through the IS-LM model. Students use algebra and graphs to explain economic behaviour and apply models to economic issues.
selectedCourses.contribution: provides economic foundations on firms, markets, incentives and macroeconomic conditions
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.

selectedCourses.name: International Macroeconomics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines short-, medium- and long-run macroeconomic dynamics and policy, including international dimensions. Students study goods, financial and labour markets, inflation and unemployment, economic growth, expectations and the open economy. IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models connect markets and policy effects. Algebraic and graphical analysis and interpretation of macroeconomic indicators support the evaluation of economic developments and fiscal and monetary policy.
selectedCourses.contribution: examines growth, inflation, business cycles and policy shaping the international business environment
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Study the economy as a whole through topics such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment. Understand how governments and central banks use fiscal and monetary policies to influence economic performance over time. The course also explores business cycles, international trade, and economic crises, preparing students to evaluate policy debates and global economic trends.

selectedCourses.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Develops microeconomic theory through consumer behaviour, imperfectly competitive markets and economy-wide allocation. Students examine choice under uncertainty, non-egoistic preferences and cognitive limitations, then monopoly, strategic behaviour and labour and capital markets. General equilibrium, efficiency, externalities and government complete the analysis. Algebraic problem-solving and graphical analysis are connected to the interpretation and evaluation of research papers.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops microeconomic and behavioural analysis of consumer and firm decisions
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity. Explore key concepts such as rational choice, decision-making under uncertainty, and non-egoistic preferences. Analyze market structures, strategic interactions, and factor markets. Learn how markets function and examine the impact of regulation. Develop analytical tools to better understand behavior and engage with empirical research.

selectedCourses.name: Public Economics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines government intervention through the efficiency and equity effects of public policy. Market failure, public goods and externalities provide foundations for studying public production, collective choice, spending and taxation. Health, education, welfare and social insurance illustrate expenditure and redistribution questions. Students apply economic models, interpret data and graphs, evaluate research and develop a research proposal and paper.
selectedCourses.contribution: examines market failure, externalities, taxation and public intervention affecting firms
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.

selectedCourses.name: Econometrics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.
selectedCourses.contribution: provides econometric tools for causal and predictive analysis of business data
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

selectedCourses.name: Behavioral Economics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.
selectedCourses.contribution: examines biases, heuristics and framing in economic and financial decision-making
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.

selectedCourses.name: Consumer Product Design
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Teaches consumer-product design and development through projects that progress from understanding an existing product to creating a new one. Students investigate product mechanisms and environmental impact, interview potential customers, translate needs into specifications, select concepts, and develop production plans and prototypes where feasible. The final project integrates these stages with industrial scaling and elementary economic analysis. Sustainability, including material use, repairability, lifespan and circularity, informs design decisions throughout.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops product innovation through customer needs, design, costing and team development
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.

selectedCourses.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Connects marketing strategy and consumer psychology to responsible brand development and customer engagement. Students study strategic planning, customer experience, qualitative and quantitative insights, brand identity, digital marketing and behavioural framing. Applied projects analyze a company's strategy and response to disruption, design a brand, and investigate a consumer phenomenon using academic literature and primary and secondary evidence. Customer-journey mapping translates findings into recommendations.
selectedCourses.contribution: examines marketing strategy, consumer psychology and responsible customer engagement
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Marketing & Consumer Engagement examines consumer psychology, marketing strategy, responsible brand development and customer engagement. Students analyse a company strategy, design a brand and investigate a consumer phenomenon using academic literature and primary and secondary evidence. Digital marketing and customer-journey mapping connect analysis with practical recommendations.

selectedCourses.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops business strategy from vision to execution and responsible digital transformation
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.

selectedCourses.name: Market Research

Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas. Ready to turn curiosity into career skills? Perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.

selectedCourses.name: International Business & Governance
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines how international trade, globalization and political, sociocultural and technological forces shape firms' cross-border decisions. Economic foundations include trade theories, foreign direct investment, foreign exchange and the monetary system. Students analyze governance, responsibility and trade-policy conflicts, investigate an international-business question, and develop an evidence-based market-entry strategy covering country attractiveness and business functions. A tariff case applies game theory to stakeholder choices and negotiation.
selectedCourses.contribution: examines institutions, culture, governance and corporate responsibility in global business
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: This course examines the institutional, political and cultural forces shaping global businesses. It first explores how international companies operate, then centers on key global challenges including cross-border governance, corporate responsibility, geopolitical strategies and global trade. It provides a comprehensive understanding of today’s complex international business environment.

selectedCourses.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces entrepreneurship and core business functions through the development of a startup concept. Students use design thinking to discover customer needs, define a problem, generate and prototype solutions, and construct value propositions and business models. Marketing, finance, operations, human resources and funding inform a coherent business plan and investor pitch. Entrepreneurial cases and a startup simulation examine decision-making, early growth and business lifecycles, with attention to societal impact and sustainability.
selectedCourses.contribution: provides business foundations while developing venture creation, business models and market validation
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.

selectedCourses.name: Research Methods & Statistics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.
selectedCourses.contribution: provides research design, surveys, experiments and statistical analysis for management questions
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

selectedCourses.name: Personal Leadership
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces leadership through self-leadership, leadership theory and emotional intelligence. Covey's habits provide a framework for personal vision, prioritization and collaboration, alongside transformational, authentic, situational and adaptive leadership perspectives. Students analyze personality and emotional-intelligence profiles in relation to group dynamics, examine leadership cases, and construct a personal development plan with actionable goals. Assessment tools support educational reflection rather than diagnosis, and the outline acknowledges differences in their scientific support.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops leadership theory, self-awareness and applied leadership practice
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Personal Leadership provides a comprehensive introduction to leadership theory and practice, designed to help students discover their unique leadership style through self-awareness and practical skill-building. Through interactive workshops, reflective exercises, and real-world applications, students engage deeply with core leadership principles and develop the tools needed to lead confidently in any setting.

selectedCourses.name: Leadership Communication
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Studies leadership communication through leadership theory, persuasion and practical rhetorical work. Students compare contemporary leadership approaches and examine emotional intelligence, gender, culture and ethics. Literary characters, film and speeches provide material for analyzing effective and ineffective leadership. Students interview a real leader, analyze the leader's communication challenge in an advisory report, and develop a public address presenting their own ethical leadership vision.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops leadership communication, ethical influence and persuasive practice
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: This course blends theory with practice from both fiction and the real world, helping you develop essential leadership skills. Learn how to inspire teams, sharpen your communication, take ethical decisions, and lead with confidence.

selectedCourses.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, emotional expression and suppression, emotional labor, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership and social interaction under conflict, exclusion and interpersonal uncertainty. It emphasises inclusive leadership and ethnic, cultural, sexual and gender minority experiences, with digital emotion regulation as a further strand. Students conduct a supervised quantitative survey project: formulating theory-driven hypotheses, selecting established psychological measures, designing and piloting a Qualtrics survey, recruiting participants ethically, collecting original data and preparing a clean dataset. Individual work applies descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression in SPSS or RStudio, and interprets findings and limitations in empirical reports and evidence-based leadership recommendations.
selectedCourses.contribution: Examines emotion regulation, belonging, identity safety and inclusive leadership under pressure, with a supervised minority/inclusion survey and empirical analysis. This is not a broad HR recruitment/reward or diversity-management sequence.
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership in diverse contexts, with particular attention to minority experiences. Students design and pilot a quantitative survey, collect data ethically, and use SPSS or RStudio for descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression. They interpret the findings and develop evidence-based leadership recommendations.

selectedCourses.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines organizational behaviour at individual, group and organizational levels. Topics connect personality, perception, emotions and motivation to teams, leadership, power, conflict, structure, culture and change. Students design research plans for organizational cases and conduct a brief systematic literature review using PRISMA reporting tools. Workshops develop literature searching, study selection, source appraisal and synthesis, linking organizational-psychology evidence to practical questions and recommendations.
selectedCourses.contribution: examines motivation, groups, organisational culture and structures through organisational psychology
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics of organisations. Case discussions and research-based frameworks address motivation, leadership, group dynamics, organisational culture, power, conflict and change.

selectedCourses.name: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Develops negotiation as an analytical practice and interpersonal skill. Students learn interest-based bargaining, BATNA and ZOPA, value creation, framing, concessions and strategies for handling power, emotions and difficult counterparts. Social-psychological and communication perspectives connect negotiation to trust, ethics, culture and relationships. Frequent simulations and narrative analysis lead to an annotated negotiation film and the design, teaching and evaluation of a negotiation scenario grounded in Delta Climate Center themes.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops negotiation, strategic interaction and analytical decision-making
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: How do you get to yes? In this course you will learn how to craft persuasive arguments, deploy the right language, negotiate more effectively, and influence decisions with confidence—whether in business, leadership, or life.

selectedCourses.name: AI Ethics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Examines AI through ethical theory and psychological accounts of human behaviour and interaction. Ethical debates address fairness, privacy, responsibility, alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Psychological perspectives consider development, clinical care, social and organizational relationships, forensic applications and cognitive neuroscience. Students synthesize literature and apply ethical frameworks in an analytical psychology project and a research-grounded podcast, with a creative communication component.
selectedCourses.contribution: AI fairness, privacy, responsibility, moral status and psychological interaction provide a defined technology-ethics inquiry; this is not a general global-business ethics course.
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness, privacy, responsibility, human-value alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Students apply ethical frameworks to questions about human behaviour and interaction, synthesise research in an analytical psychology project, and produce a research-based podcast.

selectedCourses.name: Database Management Systems
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces relational database management systems and SQL. Covers relational database theory, authorization, normalization and query processing.
selectedCourses.contribution: Relational theory, SQL, normalization, authorization and query processing supply actual information-management tools. Complementary organisational-data infrastructure; no financial database project is assumed.
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Introduces relational database management systems and SQL. Covers relational database theory, authorization, normalization and query processing.

selectedCourses.name: Algorithms & Data Structures
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Studies algorithm design and analysis, emphasizing how algorithms and data structures affect execution time. Students examine sorting, searching, random-number generation, string matching and graph algorithms, then study computability, verification, reductions and complexity classes. Programming and mathematical exercises develop algorithmic understanding, while projects require students to design, execute and report experimental investigations of performance.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops algorithmic problem-solving and data structures needed for computational business applications
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Teaches design and analysis of algorithms and data structures, emphasizing performance analysis and focusing on prominent algorithms and data structures.

selectedCourses.name: Introduction to Data Science
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces data analysis and visualization in R through practical work with tabular, textual and spatial data. Students import, clean, transform and join data, explore patterns, and construct visualizations using tidy-data principles and the grammar of graphics. Web scraping and basic programming functions extend the workflow. A student research project applies these tools to a question using data from a field of interest.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops data cleaning, visualisation and manipulation for evidence-based business analysis
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.

selectedCourses.name: Machine Learning
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces statistical learning for understanding data and predicting outcomes. Students study regression and classification, model accuracy, resampling, regularization, nonlinear models, trees, support vector machines and unsupervised learning. Practical assignments evaluate methods on real data using R or Python. Projects emphasize informative predictor construction, test-set prediction, appropriate model choice and clear reporting of results and limitations.
selectedCourses.contribution: Regression/classification, validation and model choice support prediction and evidence analysis. Real-data assignments are not assumed to use a business or financial dataset.
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Machine Learning introduces methods for understanding data and making predictions, including linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. Real-world examples illustrate the methods, their strengths and limitations.

Students build and train simple networks before studying multilayer architectures, backpropagation, regularization and model evaluation. Later work applies deep learning to computer vision, time series and text, including transformers. Projects construct predictors for tabular data and investigate an independently chosen image- or text-based prediction problem, with experimental results reported in a paper.
selectedCourses.contribution: develops neural-network and deep-learning methods for advanced AI applications
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Neural Networks & Deep Learning combines theory with practical Python, Keras and TensorFlow implementations. Students build and train networks, study backpropagation, regularisation and model evaluation, and apply deep learning to computer vision, time series and text, including transformers. Projects investigate prediction problems and report experimental results.

selectedCourses.name: Introduction to Programming

Students develop structured programs using branching, iteration, functions and data collections, then progress to recursion, exception handling and object-oriented programming with inheritance. Elements of logic, sets and enumeration support computational reasoning. Exercises and projects require students to write, trace, test, debug and explain programs that solve problems of moderate complexity.
selectedCourses.contribution: provides programming foundations for computational and AI-oriented business work
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Introduces programming and computer science. Covers structured programming, data constructs, testing, debugging and object‑oriented programming with Python, and develops computational problem‑solving skills.

selectedCourses.name: Mathematical Methods
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Develops single-variable calculus and related mathematical tools for modelling scientific problems. Functions, limits and differentiation lead to optimization, Taylor series, complex numbers, integration and differential equations. Students solve problems analytically and with Mathematica, including numerical approximation. A project implements, analyzes and adapts a dynamic model, requiring interpretation of its behaviour and explanation of the computational results.
selectedCourses.contribution: provides mathematical foundations for quantitative and data-driven modelling
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Mathematical Methods develops foundational techniques in differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations. Students solve problems analytically and with Mathematica. A project implements, analyses and adapts a dynamic model, requiring interpretation of its behaviour and computational results.

selectedCourses.name: Linear Algebra
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Develops linear algebra from systems of equations and matrix operations to vector spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues and orthogonality. Students study least-squares approximation, symmetric matrices, quadratic forms and singular value decomposition. Applications include discrete signals, difference equations, Markov chains, dynamical systems, graphics and principal component analysis. Mathematica exercises teach computer-algebra approaches to larger problems alongside analytical problem-solving.

selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Linear Algebra studies systems of equations, matrices, vectors, linear transformations and vector spaces. Students examine eigenvalues, orthogonality, least-squares approximation, quadratic forms and singular value decomposition. Applications include discrete signals, difference equations, Markov chains, dynamical systems, graphics and principal component analysis, with Mathematica supporting analytical problem-solving.

selectedCourses.name: Probability & Statistics
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Provides a rigorous introduction to probability and mathematical statistics, from probability spaces and random variables to multivariate distributions and statistical inference. Students study estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests and maximum-likelihood methods, followed by an introduction to Bayesian reasoning. Mathematica simulations verify analytical results. A substantial project implements and compares random-sampling algorithms, including inverse sampling, accept-reject sampling and Gibbs sampling.
selectedCourses.contribution: provides probability, statistical inference and simulation foundations for risk and analytics
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Provides a foundation in mathematical statistics. Covers probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation; uses computer algebra software to develop theoretical understanding and practical skills.

selectedCourses.name: Social Psychology
selectedCourses.evidenceRead: Introduces the scientific study of how thoughts, feelings and behaviour are shaped by other people and social situations. Social cognition, the self, influence and persuasion lead into group processes, prejudice, aggression, prosocial behaviour, attraction and close relationships. Students critically examine empirical research, synthesize findings from journal articles, formulate theory-guided questions and design a feasible study. The final project proposes research rather than conducting an empirical investigation.
selectedCourses.contribution: provides scientific analysis of social influence, group behaviour and interpersonal processes relevant to organisations and customers
selectedCourses.descriptionRead: Covers main theories, findings and principles of social psychology, emphasising its scientific approach to understanding how people’s feelings, thoughts and behaviour are influenced by the presence of others.

removedCourseEvidence.evidenceRead: Develops the mathematical foundations of intelligent-agent decisions under uncertainty. Probability and Bayesian networks support belief updating and inference, while temporal models address changing environments. Decision theory, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems connect uncertainty to policies and expected utility. Multi-agent decisions introduce strategic and collective interaction, and probabilistic programming provides a framework for expressing models. Students work through equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.
removedCourseEvidence.finding: Actual intelligent-agent decisions, Bayesian inference, temporal/Markov/bandit models and expected utility considered; old resource-allocation/planning claim was too loose. Cross-border legal transactions more directly implement the financial/business institutional question. Retain quantitative risk methods through probability, econometrics and financial courses.

conceptJudgments: Broad IBA response has sustained business functions: venture/business models, strategy, international entry, marketing/research, accounting, finance/economics, organisational behaviour and leadership. This directly answers international firms and management beyond generic coherence. Missing specialist functions remain meaningful gaps.

Digital direction changes educational priorities to computational systems and prediction. Strategy/AI-business, organisational analysis, accounting, marketing and international governance retain actual business substance. Programming, algorithms, databases and ML/deep learning are explicit tools, not asserted prescribed business datasets.

Finance/economics direction materially studies financial statements, managerial accounting/investment appraisal, securities, banks and risk, micro/open-economy/public economics and behaviour. Probability/econometrics/data support analysis; transnational transactions and governance provide actual business institutions. Title narrowed to the finished composition; no specialist accountancy qualification or automatic computational-finance project.
implementationFinding: Seven original unavailable placements repaired. Two course replacements strengthen actual financial and business/legal substance. Money, Banking & Finance replaces rhetorical communication in the closest option: financial decisions and bank risk address a central target subject, while Leadership Communication retains a substantial communication strand. The finance option replaces intelligent-agent planning with transnational law; no old offerings restored. BENECON314 read-only row omitted trailing empty fields: parser padded them as blanks under the existing covered semester columns, without changing the workbook or inferring missing planning coverage. All course and hard-rule checks pass; advisory economics/data/linear-algebra ordering considered softly.

rationale: BENBUSI112
Financial statements, transaction recording and accounting analysis directly address financial accounting. The UCR course also includes management accounting and investment appraisal.
BENBUSI211
Business uses and consequences of AI, information and digital transformation directly address an important emerging-technology part; dedicated information-systems management is broader.
BENBUSI312
Securities, interest rates, financial markets, risk and bank decisions provide substantial finance/investment study. The UCR course also emphasizes monetary institutions.
BENENTR211
Marketing strategy, customer experience, brand development and consumer evidence directly address marketing management.
BENENTR212
Vision-to-execution strategic planning and business-model decisions directly address strategic management, with a particular digital-transformation focus.
BENENTR311

alignmentFinding: All 30 external and 34 UCR placements reconsidered. Fifteen partial substantive relationships remain. Startup foundations are not multinational strategy; data cleaning is not statistical inference; negotiation culture is not cross-cultural management; transnational contracts are not a corporate-law curriculum; AI ethics is not general global business ethics. International strategy now uses actual market-entry/FDI/trade study; research uses actual market research; foundational statistics uses explicit inference/regression. Each UCR identity and external component occurs once. Optional research is additional/unscheduled, opposite the 12-EC thesis.
